text:
maya singh: Heads-up — tenant 'healthsync' hit its Dedicated GPU pool limit around 09:12 UTC and a portion of traffic went to Hosted. We got questions from security about data isolation and variant fallback behavior.

sam chen: do we have a policy today? i thought Dedicated tenants were 'no hosted fallback' by default.

jordan park: They can be configured two ways. current default for new dedicated customers is: reject when capacity unavailable (strict_isolation=true). But a lot of long-tail customers opt into "hosted-fallback" for availability.

taylor ramos: The tricky bit: when we spill to Hosted for availability, we must ensure model variant and telemetry tags indicate "pseudonymized" mode. Security wants a guarantee that no raw PII leaves customer VPC.

maya singh: Exactly. Proposal: introduce a fallback variant that runs a minimal PII-stripper preprocessor + model variant with reduced context retention. Label in telemetry as `routing.fallback.variant=pseudonymized-hosted`. That way console shows a clear signal.

sam chen: I like telemetry labeling. Need API-level opt-in though. Can't silently downgrade customers. Maybe add header: `X-Redwood-Routing-Consent: hosted-fallback=pseudonymize` and surface it in console per-tenant.

jordan park: config snippet for tenant flag (draft):

```json
{
  "tenant": "healthsync",
  "routing": {
    "dedicated_isolation": "reject",
    "hosted_fallback": {
      "enabled": true,
      "mode": "pseudonymize"
    }
  }
}
```

taylor ramos: UX ask: in Console, show a top-level badge next to the tenant indicating the fallback mode and a clickable timeline of any fallback events (time, variant used, tokens served). Also show cost delta for those tokens.

ops-sre: +1 on timeline. We need traces correlated with `trace.routing.breakdown` so oncall can quickly see if a spike was due to a fallback. Add a metric `fallback.count` and tag with `fallback.mode` and `variant_id`.

infra-bot: alert: tenant healthsync fallback event at 2024-10-11T09:12:14Z -> pseudonymized-hosted (variant rwd-3p-pseudo-v2).

maya singh: edge case: what if tenant has `dedicated_isolation=reject` but also set `hosted_fallback.enabled=true` in the console? conflict. We should make server-side precedence deterministic: tenant-level explicit flag overrides default org policy. But require AOR approval for enabling hosted-fallback on sensitive customers.

sam chen: Agree on deterministic precedence. Also need API semantics: when we fallback we should return an envelope field in response headers: `X-Redwood-Fallback: hosted;mode=pseudonymize;variant=rwd-3p-pseudo-v2` so customers can log & audit.

jordan park: For rollout UX: expose a canary toggle that flips `hosted_fallback` for a small percent of traffic (like 2%) and surfaces quality regressions in the console against a baseline prompt suite. We already have eval hooks; wire them to the toggle.

taylor ramos: Privacy team also asked for post-fallback verification: a sampled-outputs pipeline that runs a regex PII-check and emits a red flag metric when tokens match strict patterns. Need retention rules + access controls for those samples.

ops-sre: operational concern: if many Dedicated tenants enable hosted-fallback, Hosted capacity will see a sudden delta. Consider token accounting attribution: bill fallback tokens to the tenant but flag them separately in billing UI and rate quotas. Also add a per-tenant soft cap on fallback tokens to prevent runaway cost.

maya singh: good point. console should expose a fallback budget with alerts at 50/75/90%. Also add an automatic throttle policy if budget exhausted: either reject or switch to lowest-cost variant (opt-in).

sam chen: Quick API debate: should we allow a per-request override header `X-Redwood-Allow-Fallback: true` from the client? could be useful for mobile clients willing to trade privacy for availability. But dangerous if leaked.

jordan park: If we add per-request override, require auth scope `routing:override_fallback` and log it explicitly in audit logs. No silent per-request toggles.

maya singh: next steps: 1) sam & jordan draft the server precedence and header semantics; 2) taylor starts Console mockups for fallback badge + budget panel; 3) ops-sre and infra to propose metrics/tags and quota limits; 4) privacy to define sampling rules.

taylor ramos: i'll prototype a small panel mock and drop screenshots here.

ops-sre: i'll draft metric names: `redwood.fallback.count`, `redwood.fallback.latency`, `redwood.fallback.quality_regressions` with tags `tenant`, `fallback.mode`, `variant`.

sam chen: will open an internal RFC with the header names and example responses. will cc privacy and billing.

maya singh: thanks all. we should aim to ship the initial opt-in feature behind a console flag by EOW, then do a 2-week canary. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-bot: created draft rfc doc #482: routing/fallback-policy. Link: https://redwood.internal/rfc/482
